headline: Singapore GP: Lando Norris edges Charles Leclerc by 0.058s in Friday night practice
whyCareReason: Lando Norris and Charles Leclerc trade blistering lap times under 1,600 floodlights as qualifying simulations set up an ultra-tight Marina Bay battle.
teaser: Friday 2 October in Singapore: Norris posts 1:30.727 in FP2, edging Leclerc by 0.058 seconds. Mercedes championship leader Antonelli stays within striking distance.
story:
Why this one matters: Friday night at Marina Bay confirmed that the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix is poised to become a razor-thin tactical war between McLaren and Ferrari.

Under the glare of 1,600 floodlights and through sweltering 30-degree night air, Lando Norris unleashed an electric 1:30.727 during the qualifying simulations in Free Practice 2. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, who had topped the earlier twilight session in FP1 with a 1:31.763, answered with a sensational flying lap of his own, falling short by a mere 0.058 seconds.

Carlos Sainz backed up Ferrari's pace in third, while championship leader Kimi Antonelli and George Russell slotted into fourth and fifth for Mercedes. With overtaking notoriously difficult across Marina Bay's 19 tight corners, Saturday's qualifying shootout will carry immense weight for the title fight.
stakes: Crucial pole position advantage on a street circuit where qualifying almost always dictates Sunday victory.
rivalryAngle: McLaren and Ferrari agility challenge Mercedes power on the tightest, most punishing street circuit in motorsport.
